# Clarify movable policy boundaries in the Dock Layouts guides

## Context

While checking the stage-2 Dock Layouts post, Ada observed that a pane declared `movable: false` still moves between stacks in one workspace. The current Adoption guide describes model-enforced policies, but its declaration comment and Common integration mistakes can be read as a promise that this flag prevents every move.

This is a bounded v13.2 documentation correction. It does not decide a broader engine policy.

## The Problem

Readers need to distinguish a cross-document transfer restriction from an in-workspace position lock. The detailed policy example already names cross-document transfer; the surrounding general language leaves that distinction implicit.

## The Architectural Reality

At dev `4bf45e51e4`, `src/dashboard/dock/model/Operations.mjs` checks `movable === false` in `transferItem` and `transferNode`. `moveItem` does not check that flag. The existing transfer refusal tests are in `DockZoneModel.spec.mjs`.

Independent single-thread probes with the real Operations executor confirmed:
- Valid source and target documents; `moveItem(console, right)` returns no errors and places the pane in the right stack despite `movable: false`.
- `transferItem` refuses with `item "console" is not movable`, retaining both input documents.
- `transferNode` refuses the same member; the same descriptor succeeds when its flag is true.

Design authority: the guide says “the honest way to teach them is by what the model actually refuses.” This ticket corrects that description against executed behavior; it does not call local movement wrong or claim the asymmetry is a settled universal design rule.

Decision Record impact: none — no engine or ADR change. Structure map: N/A, two existing guide files.

## The Fix

In `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsAdoption.md`, make the declaration comment, Decision 3 and integration advice name the cross-document boundary and explicitly state that the flag does not freeze in-workspace position. Keep the overview in `DockLayouts.md` consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The two guides describe `movable: false` as rejecting cross-document transfers, and the detailed guide explicitly says in-workspace moves remain possible.
- [ ] The declaration example and integration advice no longer imply a universal movement prohibition; close/pin guidance keeps its existing meaning.
- [ ] The diff changes documentation only and records the reducer probe evidence without claiming a browser or policy redesign.

## Out of Scope

Changing reducers, adding policy flags or UI guards, redefining `locked`, rewriting the stage-2 post, and the WindowPosition warning owned by #19619.
